outlook.summary: Not financial advice — this is a personal tracking dashboard meant to organize publicly available information for research purposes. Always size positions and confirm with your own research.

strongest.area: Cybersecurity & enterprise software, led by CrowdStrike, NetApp, and Salesforce
strongest.reason: the sector continues a broad rotation into AI-capable security and software platforms, with names like Tenable up over 40% year-to-date on surging exposure-management demand and Palo Alto Networks pacing a fourth straight winning session, up 110% year-over-year

strongest.area: AI infrastructure & cloud spending, led by Nvidia and record hyperscaler capex
strongest.reason: enterprise cloud-infrastructure spending hit a record $143 billion in Q2, up sharply from $100 billion the prior quarter, keeping the broader AI-buildout narrative intact even as individual mega-cap names traded mixed

weakest.area: Chips & semiconductors, particularly Alphabet, AMD, TSM, and ASML
weakest.reason: a sharp post-earnings selloff in memory-chip names (Sandisk, Western Digital) rippled through the sector, dragging SK Hynix down 10% and Samsung down 6.2% overnight in Asia and pulling AMD, TSM, and ASML lower despite still-record global semiconductor sales

weakest.area: Parts of crypto, specifically DeFi and stablecoins
weakest.reason: bitcoin and ethereum themselves held up near multi-week highs, but the broader DeFi market cap crashed nearly 39% and stablecoin market cap fell 5% over 24 hours, a notable stress signal beneath the surface

outlook.nextStep: The memory-chip-driven pullback rippling from Sandisk and Western Digital into AMD, TSM, ASML, and Asian chipmakers is the more worth a closer look story today, given how quickly sentiment flipped from this week's earlier AMD-led rally. The DeFi/stablecoin stress and Serve Robotics' upcoming earnings are more event-driven and probably better watched than acted on until clearer follow-through emerges.

signals.title: Rate-cut odds hold near 75% for September as jobs data softens
signals.body: Following last week's divided 9-3 Fed vote to hold rates steady, markets are pricing roughly 75% odds of a 25-basis-point cut in September. A weaker-than-expected ADP jobs report released today added to the case for easing, even as the S&P and Nasdaq traded near record territory.
signals.focus: worth a closer look at whether soft labor data accelerates the timeline for a Fed pivot

signals.title: Memory-chip selloff spreads from Sandisk and Western Digital into the broader sector
signals.body: Sandisk and Western Digital both fell sharply after earnings missed elevated expectations, sending shockwaves through the memory and broader semiconductor complex. SK Hynix dropped 10% and Samsung fell 6.2% overnight in Asia, and the pullback spilled into AMD, TSM, and ASML today despite global semiconductor sales posting a 15th consecutive monthly record.
signals.focus: worth a closer look at whether this is an isolated memory-sector reaction or a broader demand-sustainability concern

signals.title: Enterprise cloud-infrastructure spending hits a record $143 billion in Q2
signals.body: Cloud-infrastructure spending jumped to $143 billion in Q2 2026, up from $100 billion in Q1, reinforcing that hyperscaler AI capex remains on an accelerating trajectory even as individual cloud stocks traded mixed today, with Amazon still weighed down by the Bezos share-sale filing.
signals.focus: worth a closer look at whether capex acceleration keeps translating into stock performance for the underlying chip and cloud names

signals.title: Robotics rally builds ahead of Serve Robotics earnings
signals.body: A broad risk-on wave lifted robotics and automation names today, with Teradyne and Ouster extending recent gains ahead of Serve Robotics' Q2 report due after today's close. Industry forecasts point to the industrial robotics market growing from roughly $65 billion this year to nearly $344 billion by 2036.
signals.focus: worth a closer look at how the group reacts once Serve Robotics reports tonight

signals.title: Enterprise software mixed as Palantir cools further from its earnings peak
signals.body: Palantir eased again as profit-taking continues following its outsized post-earnings rally, while Salesforce outperformed on a broader software-sector bid and ServiceNow and Adobe traded close to flat.
signals.focus: worth a closer look at whether Palantir's pullback is simple profit-taking or an early sentiment shift

signals.title: Bitcoin and ethereum firm near multi-week highs, but DeFi and stablecoins show stress
signals.body: Bitcoin and ethereum both firmed on continued Hormuz de-escalation hopes and a three-day, $626 million streak of spot Bitcoin ETF inflows. Beneath the surface, however, the broader DeFi market cap crashed nearly 39% and the stablecoin market cap fell 5% over the past 24 hours, a divergence worth watching.
signals.focus: lower conviction right now on anything DeFi-adjacent until the cause of the crash is better understood

signals.title: Cybersecurity rally continues as AI-driven threat demand accelerates
signals.body: CrowdStrike jumped further and the broader cybersecurity group remains strong, with Tenable up more than 40% year-to-date on surging exposure-management demand as attackers increasingly use AI to find vulnerabilities faster, and Palo Alto Networks pacing a fourth consecutive winning session.
signals.focus: worth a closer look given the string of positive fundamental catalysts continuing across the group
